items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: When I was with the Benny Carter band, we only used one mic. And I sang with that band too. I sang “I Can’t Get Started” or whatever that was popular. And we had the great Maxine Sullivan.

ctx.x: Benny. Benny Carter was a perfectionist. And he was someone to be looked up to because he was such a great musician. As a matter of fact he was such a great trumpet player until all the trumpet players that ever worked with him looked up to him. He wasn’t that strict you know what I mean? I’m 83, Benny is about 90 I would say, around 90 years old. But I celebrated my 21st birthday with Benny in North Carolina with Benny. He treated me all right. You know what I mean? As a matter of fact I could say this for…

I’m looking down on the Hudson River, and I said, “Pardon me” — he was a banjo player in a Dixieland band. And I said, “Where did you ever hear that song?” He said, “That was Benny Carter’s opening number 48 years ago, named ‘Pom Pom.’” He says to me, “I could hum everything that Benny Carter ever played, and I never — I wanted to see him and talk to him, but that was out of the way.” And during those days now, you’ve got to remember, we didn’t have any microphones. When I was with the Benny Carter band, we only…
Picked it up and did a cover of it or something.
